cosy-lesson.title: "Knowledge isn't free. You have to pay attention.": Richard Feynman

cosy-teacher-notes.p: Stage aim: to introduce the topic and clarify key target vocabulary for the session.

cosy-slide.cosy-instruction: Review the key vocabulary for this session below:

cosy-blockquote.p: Inquisitiveness – having or showing an interest in learning things; curious.

p.em: Example: His natural inquisitiveness drove him to take apart old watches to see how they worked.

cosy-blockquote.p: Vigilance – the action or state of keeping careful watch for possible danger or difficulties.

p.em: Example: We must maintain constant mental vigilance to avoid falling for misinformation online.

cosy-blockquote.p: Complacency – a feeling of smug or uncritical satisfaction with oneself or one's achievements.

p.em: Example: We cannot afford complacency when it comes to keeping our skills updated.

cosy-blockquote.p: Cognitive – relating to the mental action or process of acquiring knowledge and understanding.

p.em: Example: Sleep deprivation has a severe negative impact on our cognitive stamina.

cosy-blockquote.p: Disruptive – causing or tending to cause disruption or unsettling focus.

p.em: Example: Notifications are highly disruptive to deep study sessions.

cosy-blockquote.p: Preserve – to maintain something in its original or existing state.

p.em: Example: Reading physical books helps preserve our capacity for long-term concentration.

cosy-blockquote.p: Rigor – the quality of being extremely thorough, exhaustive, or accurate.

p.em: Example: Scientific research demands absolute academic rigor to verify hypotheses.

cosy-blockquote.p: Assimilate – take in and fully understand information or ideas.

p.em: Example: It takes years of practice to properly assimilate the nuances of a foreign language.

cosy-blockquote.p: Cursory – hasty and therefore not thorough or detailed.

p.em: Example: A cursory reading of the headline is never enough to understand the full article.
Example: Active participation is indispensable if you want to become fluent in a language.

cosy-teacher-notes.p: Stage aim: pair/group discussion on core session themes.

cosy-slide.cosy-group-instruction: In pairs or small breakout groups, discuss the following questions:

ol.li:
How does a child's natural inquisitiveness conflict with the standardized curriculum of modern schooling?
★ Complete using inversion: 'Seldom do we discover profound truths without active questioning.'

Why does maintaining intellectual vigilance require more energy in a world flooded with automated answers?
★ How do you train yourself to spot biases in online articles?

How can we guard against intellectual complacency when search engines satisfy our queries instantly?
★ Have you ever assumed you understood a subject, only to realize you had barely scratched the surface?

In what ways does constant multitasking alter our long-term cognitive development?
★ What daily routine helps you restore your cognitive focus after a hectic day?

Should companies be held responsible for designing disruptive software that feeds on human attention?
★ Which app on your phone do you find the most disruptive to your peace of mind?

Why is it vital for our emotional health to preserve some memories without posting them online?
★ What is a precious personal memory you keep entirely to yourself?

Does the academic rigor of traditional universities prepare students for the fluid demands of the modern world?
★ When did a strict rule or hard discipline teach you a valuable life lesson?

How quickly can a community assimilate major cultural changes without losing its unique identity?
★ What aspect of modern culture do you find easiest or hardest to assimilate?

What are the social dangers of having only a cursory understanding of complex scientific breakthroughs?
★ Have you ever had to discuss a complex topic with someone who had only a cursory knowledge of it?

Why is face-to-face mentorship still an indispensable part of professional growth?
★ Who has been an indispensable guide or mentor in your professional journey?

cosy-teacher-notes.p: Stage aim: deeper debate and statement evaluation in pairs/groups.

cosy-slide.cosy-group-instruction: In pairs, debate and state whether you agree or disagree with these statements:

ol.li:
In tomorrow's society, passive complacency will be seen as a mental illness that requires active clinical therapy. : Do you agree or disagree?
★ Would you live in a society that perfectly manages your happiness at the expense of your critical thinking?

Brain-computer interfaces will allow us to instantly assimilate library databases, making school study obsolete. : Do you agree or disagree?
★ If you could instantly download a skill, which one would you choose?

Intellectual vigilance will become a high-status luxury trait only practiced by wealthy elites. : Do you agree or disagree?
★ Do you worry that deep thinking will become a privilege rather than a universal right?

Virtual realities will create perfectly focused environments with zero disruptive elements. : Do you agree or disagree?
★ Would you spend your workday inside a virtual quiet forest if it boosted your output?

Future legal frameworks will penalize tech platforms that degrade human cognitive stamina. : Do you agree or disagree?
★ Should governments limit social media usage to protect public health?

A cursory approach to reading will completely replace literature, with novels reduced to short animated summaries. : Do you agree or disagree?
★ Do you think the art of writing long books will survive the next century?

To survive in an automated world, constant creative inquisitiveness will be the only trait that guarantees job safety. : Do you agree or disagree?
★ How do you keep your curiosity alive outside of your regular work duties?

Biometric feedback will allow us to monitor and preserve our emotional states in perfect balance. : Do you agree or disagree?
★ Would you want a device to tell you when you are feeling slightly anxious?

Academic rigor will become obsolete as artificial intelligence takes over all analytical and scientific tasks. : Do you agree or disagree?
★ Do you believe AI can eventually perform better science than human researchers?

Personal wisdom is indispensable for leadership and can never be generated by artificial neural networks. : Do you agree or disagree?
★ Would you ever vote for a country leader whose decisions were entirely guided by an AI advisor?

ul.li: Incorrect: We must pay the attention → Correct: We must pay attention ((Omit 'the' in the idiom 'pay attention'))
Incorrect: I am study physics → Correct: I study physics ((Simple present structure))
Incorrect: It depend on how much effort you do → Correct: It depends on how much effort you make ((Collocation 'make an effort', singular verb))
